brief.headline: Salvador has new evening confusion (including a stove left on) that began about two weeks before 2026-11-03, shortly after apixaban was started on 2026-10-24. He has also lost 8.4% of his weight since 2026-09-05.

items.statement: On 2026-11-03 the RN recorded that his caregiver Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. He was oriented to person and place but not date, and had no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. The notes in this packet do not show results or the PCP visit.
items.verifier_note: The confusion, stove, orientation, no fever and plan all match the note. The note names Marcus but never says he is the caregiver, so that role is unsupported.

items.statement: Weight fell from 83.4 kg on 2026-09-05 to 76.4 kg on 2026-11-24, a loss of 7.0 kg (15.4 lb, 8.4%). The decline was steady: 80.9 kg on 10/01 and 78.5 kg on 10/28. On 11/24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The weights, the 7.0 kg / 15.4 lb / 8.4% change, and the intermediate readings match the vitals record. The dietitian note supports the appetite findings and the plan. The note rounds the loss to 8%.

items.statement: Apixaban 5 mg was started on 2026-10-24 for new atrial fibrillation found on ECG. The pharmacist reconciled it on 10/26 and updated the blister pack. He also takes clopidogrel. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks, which falls around 11/21, and no recheck is documented in these notes.
items.verifier_note: The apixaban start, the indication, the pharmacist reconciliation and blister pack update, and the 4-week recheck are supported. The notes document no recheck, which fits the statement. Clopidogrel appears in none of the cited sources, so that detail is unsupported.

items.statement: The stove was left on once at home, per caregiver Marcus on 2026-11-03. This is a home safety concern alongside the new evening confusion.
items.verifier_note: The note supports the stove being left on once and the evening confusion. It does not identify Marcus as a caregiver. Calling it a home safety concern is the drafter's inference, not something the note states.

Route to prescriber for review.

Check the medication list for duplication: two simvastatin entries (10 mg started 2026-01-25 and 20 mg started 2009-10-04) are both active. Verify whether the 20 mg was stopped or replaced, whether the 10 mg start was an intentional switch, and whether the active list is accurate; confirm which strength the participant is actually taking.

Falls and injury review for the window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30): given brain injury history, new anticoagulation, and osteoporosis on alendronate, pull all fall incidents, near-falls, head injuries, and any fracture work-up. Check fall-risk screening and whether post-fall review occurred.

ED visits and hospital admissions in the window, including any related to AF symptoms, chest pain (ischemic heart disease), bleeding, or neurologic events; confirm discharge summaries are on file and any med changes from them were reconciled.

Medication starts and stops since last review: confirm alendronic acid 10 mg (started 2026-01-04) adherence and administration instructions (upright positioning, fasting), check for any missed doses, and confirm metoprolol succinate 100 mg, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, and simvastatin remain as intended with no unexplained discontinuations.

Cardiac monitoring: review heart rate and rhythm documentation, blood pressure trend, and any symptoms (palpitations, dizziness, dyspnea, angina use of nitroglycerin spray). Check whether nitroglycerin use frequency has changed.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+): compare recorded weights across the window with the prior review, note any unintentional change, and check nutrition and dietary-counseling documentation.

Lipid and cardiometabolic monitoring for hyperlipidemia and ischemic heart disease: check for any lipid panel results, LDL trend, and whether the statin regimen change was followed by a documented lab recheck.

Cognition, mood, function, and caregiver: screen for changes in cognition given prior brain injury, mood/depression and attendance at PACE center, ADL/IADL status, and caregiver or home-situation changes; also confirm any care-plan items due in the window (reassessments, care-plan review date, osteoporosis bone-density or fracture-prevention follow-up) are completed or overdue.
